service.description: Runs the DeviceRequest named by the query of a routing request, as the dispatch-device-request route of the Camel gateway did: DeviceServices.run#DeviceRequest with that requestName, so on its runServiceName or on the driver of its connection. Set as the runServiceName of the routing request.

return.message: DeviceRequest ${request.requestName} (deviceId=${request.deviceId}) is missing query. Set query to the requestName of the DeviceRequest to run.

service.description:
Renders the recipe of a DeviceRuleSet as text files, one per DeviceRule priority, named ruleSetName_pNN.txt. Each line is name:=value, sorted by name.
Parameter lines: the Parameter records of the DeviceConfig of each DeviceRule. The name is the requestItemName of a DeviceRequestItem of the Parameter when there is one; otherwise it depends on DeviceConfig.deviceTypeEnumId: DtPLC gives dev.alias, DtMoquiPlc* gives dev.deviceName.alias, any other type gives the alias, or deviceName.parameterName. The alias is Parameter.parameterAlias, or ParameterDef.parameterName; deviceName is PhysicalDevice.deviceName, or the deviceId of the rule. The value is numericValue, else parameterEnumId, else symbolicValue.
Trajectory lines, when the DeviceConfig has an approximatedFunctionId: Trajectory.trajectoryId, Trajectory.pointCount and, for each TrajectoryPoint (index sequenceNum - 1), Trajectory.points[i].pos.v[d] (VectorComponent.realValue), .sequenceNum, .timeOffsetMs, .isBreakPoint, .hasBlendingOverride, .bufferMode and .transitionMode (from blendingEnumId), .blendingMode (ParametricPathPoint.tolerance).

parameter.name: deviceId
parameter.description: Only the rules of this device.

parameter.name: files
parameter.description: Maps with name, content, priority and rowCount.

service.description:
Exports a device configuration recipe (Codesys txt-recipe format), as the run-device-config-export and transfer-file routes of the Camel gateway did. get#DeviceConfigExportFiles renders one file per DeviceRule priority, {ruleSetName}_p{priority:02d}.txt, with one name:=value line per parameter.
The files go to the DeviceConnection of requestName: its transportConfig, file:directory or sftp://host:port/directory, with its options (see transfer#DeviceContent). Without a connection they go to the location in the property device_config_export_location and, when set, device_config_export_location_2 (file.transfer.uri and file.transfer.uri.2 of the Camel gateway). The result is notified with DeviceServices.receive#GatewayRequestCallback: exportCompleted, or writeFailed.
Persistent trajectories (one Parameter per axis per waypoint, under a dedicated DeviceRuleSet) are exported by this same service; export#Trajectory is the ephemeral path.

parameter.name: deviceId
parameter.description: Optional. When set, limits the export to parameters belonging to this device's rules only.

parameter.name: deviceRuleId
parameter.description: Optional. When set, limits the export to a single DeviceRule. Can be combined with deviceId for more specific filtering.

parameter.name: requestName
parameter.description: The DeviceRequest of the export (requestTypeEnumId DrtConfigWrite).

parameter.name: files
parameter.description: Maps with name, priority and rowCount.

return.message: DeviceRuleSet ${deviceRuleSetId} has no parameters or trajectory points to export.
DeviceConnection ${request.connectionName} of request ${requestName} has no transportConfig destination.
DeviceRequest ${requestName} has no destination: set its DeviceConnection, or the property device_config_export_location.

service-call.name: moqui.device.DeviceServices.receive#GatewayRequestCallback

log.message: DeviceConfig export of rule set ${deviceRuleSetId} with request ${requestName}: ${status}, ${files.length} file(s), ${rowCount} line(s)

service.description: The destination of a file transfer DeviceRequest: its brokerUri, else the transportConfig of its DeviceConnection, with the options of the connection.

return.message: DeviceRequest ${requestName} has no destination: set its brokerUri or the transportConfig of its DeviceConnection.

service.description: The file of a DeviceContent, read through the resource facade, for a DrtContentTransfer DeviceRequest of the same device: a list with one map of name and bytes.

Transfers the file of a DeviceContent (G-Code, CNC program, firmware, recipe, ...) to a device, as the transfer-device-content route of the Camel gateway did. The file is read from DeviceContent.contentLocation through the resource facade and written to the destination of the DrtContentTransfer DeviceRequest named by the query of requestName, or of requestName itself when it has no query.
Destination (DeviceRequest.brokerUri, else DeviceConnection.transportConfig): file:directory, written through the resource facade, or sftp://host:port/directory, written with SftpClient. SFTP options, in DeviceConnection.options or the query of the destination: host-key-fingerprint (SHA256:..., required), username and password or private-key-file; usernameEnv and passwordEnv name an environment variable instead.

Reads the waypoints of a planned trajectory (ApproximatedFunctionSample in sequenceNum order, each with its VectorComponent values) and returns one value list per axis. Axis names follow the vector space of the ApproximatedFunction: X,Y,Z,A,B,C for EngTcpPose6Dof, J1..J6 otherwise; a dimension beyond the sixth is named D and its index. TrajectoryAxisBinding is not used: this is the planned waypoint stream as it is.

return.message: Trajectory ${approximatedFunctionId} has an incomplete or invalid waypoint vector.
Trajectory ${approximatedFunctionId} has a missing or non-finite coordinate.

service.description:
Publishes a planned trajectory for immediate execution (the ephemeral path; a recipe exported with export#DeviceConfig is the persistent one). The waypoints of the ApproximatedFunction (get#TrajectoryAxes) go out as one JSON message through DeviceServices.run#DeviceRequest: the DeviceRequest is an MQTT write without items whose brokerUri is the broker and whose query is the topic that MqttParameterSub on the PLC subscribes to; JsonToParametersMapper there expects the keys X,Y,Z,A,B,C (TCP pose) or J1..J6 (joint space).
Message: {"requestName": "ROBOT_ARM_TRAJECTORY_EXPORT", "approximatedFunctionId": "100051", "waypointCount": 10, "mqttTopic": "moqui/robot/arm1/trajectory", "axes": {"X": [850.0, 860.0], "Y": [0.0, 20.0]}}

return.message: DeviceRequest ${requestName} has no query: set it to the MQTT topic.

service.description: An inbound error or recovery of a request (eventType inboundError or inboundRecovered), as the Camel gateway sent it to this service over REST. The sample store now tells the users itself (FieldbusServices.notify#InboundState); this service does the same for a caller that still sends the event.

log.message: Gateway notification ${eventType} on route ${routeId} (${protocol}) without a known request: ${errorMessage}
